one_liner: A paid spring internship supporting the Library of Congress's COIL international exchange programs, covering outreach, event logistics, participant correspondence, data entry and reports.
fit_summary: Your policy knowledge, people skills and government-client consulting work at IEM fit the outreach, stakeholder and congressional-liaison side of this role well. The hard gate is education: applicants must currently be pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree, with at least junior standing for undergraduates, and nothing on file shows you are enrolled. If you are not enrolled, you cannot qualify.
eligibility: Must be currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree at an accredited school; undergraduates need junior-level standing (third year or above) when they apply.
Open to the public; requires U.S. citizenship or other eligibility under Title VII, Sec. 704 of the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2022.
Must pass a background investigation and maintain Public Trust eligibility.
This is an Excepted Service internship with no competitive status and no promotion potential.
strategy: First confirm you are enrolled in a degree program and can document it, such as with a transcript or enrollment letter. If you are not, skip this posting and look for entry-level Legislative Branch or state jobs instead.

Describe your IEM work in terms of government-client coordination, stakeholder communication, logistics for meetings or exercises, and report drafting. Use only duties you actually performed, with dates and hours per week.

Show your policy knowledge and Capitol Hill familiarity as an ability to work with Congressional staff. Mention any Hill, campaign or advocacy contacts, since Legislative Branch experience is preferred.
Selection is resume-based with interviews, not a questionnaire, so keep to two pages and mirror the posting's duty language closely.
Apply between Oct 23 and Nov 6, 2026, and plan for an in-person commute from Manassas, since the role has no telework.
resume_bullets: Coordinated [meetings/exercises/events] for [number] government client stakeholders at IEM, managing schedules, materials and follow-up communication.
Drafted [summaries/reports/correspondence] documenting [topic, participation or outcomes] for [client/supervisor], following established formats.
Entered and tracked [type of data] in [Excel/system name] to produce [reports] for [audience], ensuring accuracy under tight deadlines.
interview_questions: Tell us about a time you juggled several unrelated tasks under deadline. How did you keep accuracy high?
How would you communicate with a congressional staffer about program details while knowing when to refer questions to senior staff?
Describe an event or program you helped coordinate, including a problem you spotted and how you handled it.
Why are you interested in international exchange and COIL's mission of connecting emerging leaders with Congress?
watch_outs: The degree-enrollment requirement is disqualifying if you are not currently a student.
This is a temporary spring internship with no promotion potential and no competitive status, so it will not convert into a career position.
No telework is allowed, which means a daily commute from Manassas to DC.
